images.title: Centre of the square
images.purpose: Show that the centre of a square is where its two diagonals cross, and a circle centred there fits inside.
images.composition: One large square centred with two grey diagonals and one circle; wide white margins.
images.exact_structure: One square of side 6 cm, outline teal #0072B2, with its two diagonals as grey #6B7280 lines crossing at point O. A circle of radius 2 cm centred exactly at O, outline reddish purple #CC79A7, lying wholly inside the square, with white gap to each side. Dot at O. Exactly 1 square, 2 diagonals, 1 circle, 1 dot.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a circle centred on a side or crossing the edge of the square
images.takeaway: The compass point goes where the two diagonals cross.
images.description: Square of side 6 cm with two diagonals meeting at O and a circle of radius 2 cm centred at O inside it.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at where the diagonals cross and say the compass point goes there.

image_decisions.why: One clean geometry picture carries the single idea of this video.
